defaults.time: timeoutMs 10,000 ms wall clock per exec or wait call (clamp 100-60,000), shared by worker preparation, guest work and inline tool waits; approval waits pause it. Pending tool calls can instead return status 'waiting' for a later wait with a fresh budget (src/agents/code-mode-runtime.ts:110; docs/tools/code-mode/configuration.md).
defaults.output: maxOutputBytes 64 KiB shared by output entries, value and error across waits (clamp 1 KiB-10 MiB); over the cap a {truncated, omittedBytes, guidance, prefix} marker replaces the item. Console: each string clipped to 512 UTF-16 units with '…[truncated]', 16,384 units per cell then '[console output truncated]' (code-mode-runtime.ts:112; code-mode-controller-source.ts:101-115; code-mode-json.ts:93). A trailing expression returns null; only `return` sets the value.
defaults.tool_calls: maxPendingToolCalls 16 in flight (clamp 1-128); further calls queue in the guest, up to 128 queued ordinary calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:114; code-mode-controller-source.ts:12, :227-230; code-mode-worker-types.ts:10). No per-exec total call cap was found on the exec path: 40 calls ran. Headless scripts default to 5 calls (code-mode-runtime.ts:26).
defaults.memory: memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB, applied as the Worker's V8 resourceLimits (maxOldGenerationSizeMb = 60, maxYoungGenerationSizeMb = 4) plus a GC-pressure watchdog that fails the cell with runtime_unavailable and retires the worker. Not an RSS limit: external buffers are excluded, and up to eight warm workers may be kept (code-mode-node.ts:234-238; docs/tools/code-mode/executors.md).

source_notes.finding: Every catalog-eligible tool becomes an async global function (callableName) plus a callable handle; bindings come from createCodeModeCatalogBindings. The model sees a bounded quick index of `name input -> output` hints built from JSON Schema, capped at 8,000 chars, and TypeScript-style declarations through API.list/API.read. Executable cells are plain JavaScript; TypeScript syntax and require/import are rejected before execution.

Hidden catalog, searched on demand: only exec and wait (plus required direct-only tools) are model-visible (telemetry visibleTools [exec, wait] in every result). Tools past the 8,000-char index are reachable through catalog.search(query) (BM25 lexical index, default 8 results, max 50) and handle.describe(). Scales past 100 tools without putting every schema in the prompt.

Guest calls go through the controller's request() into a host callback that carries only strings (method, JSON args, id, stack); the host runs the call through runtime.callExactValue, the same tool execution path as normal turns (policy, approvals, before_tool_call hooks). Replies are queued on the host and pulled by the guest (__openclawSettleBridge). Node: host function __openclawHostRequest installed on the vm context and deleted from globals after the controller captures it.

node:vm context (createContext(Object.create(null)), microtaskMode afterEvaluate, dynamic import rejected) in a worker_threads Worker with env {} and V8 heap resourceLimits. The docs say plainly that this is NOT a security boundary. The code adds one concrete hole: the host realm's TextEncoder/TextDecoder classes are injected into the context and wrapped by guest classes that hold the host instance in a #private field (comment: 'Keep native encoding prototypes private'). Errors thrown by the host decoder (bad label, fatal decode) reach guest code unwrapped, so e.constructor.constructor is the host Function: process, child_process, fs and network follow (P12 #9-#12, P3 #3). env {} hides process.env, but `ps -E` on the gateway pid returns PROBE_SECRET.

source_notes.finding: The model gets one JSON document: status, telemetry, ordered output entries (text(), json(), console.*) and the returned value or error. Over-budget items become an explicit truncation marker with the original JSON prefix and omittedBytes, not a silent cut. Console strings are clipped to 512 units each.

All limits come from tools.codeMode (global or per agent) and are clamped in resolveCodeModeConfig: timeoutMs 10 s (100 ms-60 s), memoryLimitBytes 64 MiB (1 MiB-1 GiB), maxOutputBytes 64 KiB, maxSnapshotBytes 10 MiB, maxPendingToolCalls 16, snapshotTtlSeconds 900. For Node, memoryLimitBytes becomes the Worker's maxOldGenerationSizeMb (limit-4 MB) plus 4 MB young; a GC watchdog retires near-limit workers; the deadline is enforced by terminating the worker.

Each exec gets a fresh context (globals never carry over), confirmed by P8. Workers are pooled and reused only when cells run inside the Gateway's bound resource host; without it every Node cell starts a new worker (about 200 ms). There is opt-in persistence: store(key, value)/load(key) keep small JSON values per session across cells and restarts, but only for a session-bound run (P8 #3 fails in this harness). A suspended cell (status 'waiting') keeps its live worker and context for wait.

source_notes.finding: Guest errors return status failed with code internal_error and `Name: message` plus stack frames rewritten to openclaw-code-mode:user.js:line:col (user line numbers, wrapper removed); error text is bounded to 16,384 units. Parse errors are reported before execution with line and column. A runtime `ReferenceError: process|require|module is not defined` is rewritten into the generic 'module access is disabled' invalid_input message. Tool errors are catchable in guest code and are redacted (input shown as [redacted]).

With tools.codeMode absent, activation is 'auto': Code Mode engages automatically for catalog-preferred models (for example claude-opus-5-5, gpt-5.6, gemini-3.5-flash) with the Node executor unless executor: 'quickjs' is set. Credentials stay host-side: tools run in the Gateway with their normal auth, and the guest only receives JSON results. The lexical module check (code-mode-source.ts:226) is a usability guard, not a security control: it blocks the literal require()/import() but not Function-constructor paths.

surprises: The guest-API docs say TextEncoder/TextDecoder 'provide local byte conversion, not filesystem, module, or network access' (docs/tools/code-mode/guest-api.md:50-52). Under the Node executor they are the escape: errors thrown by the injected host-realm decoder carry the host Function constructor, so guest code gets process, child_process, fs and network. The wrapper hides the host prototypes (code-mode-node.worker.ts:155-182) but not the host errors.

The docs are honest that node:vm is 'not a security boundary', but it is the default executor, and with tools.codeMode absent Code Mode engages automatically ('auto') for preferred models such as claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-5.6. A default install with a preferred model therefore runs model-written code in an escapable context inside the Gateway process.
Worker env {} hides process.env from an escaped cell, but `ps -E` on the shared pid still returns the Gateway's environment, PROBE_SECRET included.
A runtime 'process is not defined' is reported as invalid_input 'code mode module access is disabled' with failurePhase 'input', although the code had already run.
Without the Gateway's bound resource host every Node cell spawns a new worker (median 253 ms); inside it, cells reuse warm workers (median 0.95 ms). Direct callers of the exec tool pay the cold path.
At memoryLimitBytes 16 MiB, a trivial concurrent `return 42` cell failed once (1 of 3 runs) with 'worker exhausted its 16 MiB JavaScript heap' while another cell was spinning.
A trailing expression yields null (documented in the exec schema), so the SPEC's P2 form returns no value; only `return` does.
